data.name: Tacos de Rajas con Crema
data.description: Smoky poblano strips and sweet sautéed onions nestle in silky, lightly tangy Mexican crema. Warm corn tortillas cradle the tender filling, bringing toasted corn aroma to every bite.

refrigerator.notes: Store filling separately from tortillas in a shallow, covered container at 4°C (40°F) or colder. Refrigerate within 2 hours, or within 1 hour when the ambient temperature exceeds 32°C (90°F).

freezer.notes: Freezing is not recommended because the crema can separate and the peppers soften.

storage.reheating: Reheat the filling gently in a saucepan, stirring until it reaches 74°C (165°F) throughout on a food thermometer. Warm tortillas separately and assemble just before eating. Temperature guidance: [FoodSafety.gov](https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/safe-minimum-internal-temperatures).

items.name: poblano peppers
items.notes: Edible flesh target after roasting, peeling and removing stems and seeds. Buy approximately 650–700 g whole poblanos, usually 5–6 medium peppers; expected prepared yield is approximately 500 g.

items.name: mexican crema
items.notes: Use Mexican crema made with pasteurized dairy.

items.name: salt
items.notes: Starting amount for unsalted crema; if the crema tastes salty, add only part of this measured amount initially.

items.name: corn tortillas
items.notes: 12 small tortillas weighing approximately 25 g each. Choose tortillas made without wheat.

instructions.text: Preheat the broiler to high, approximately 260°C (500°F), with the rack 10–15 cm below the element. Allow about 3 minutes while preparing the peppers.
Cut the washed poblanos lengthwise into broad panels, removing stems, seeds and pale inner ribs. Place the panels skin-side up on the baking sheet in a single layer.
Broil the poblano panels for 7–9 minutes, until most of the skin is blackened and blistered. Watch closely near the end; the flesh should soften without drying out.

doneness_cues.visual: Most of the skin is blistered with broad blackened patches.
doneness_cues.tactile: The panels bend readily when lifted with tongs.

tips: Prepare and measure the onion, crema and tortillas while the peppers broil.

instructions.text: Rest the hot peppers in the heatproof bowl with its lid on for 5 minutes to loosen their skins. Cook the onions during this interval.
Sauté the sliced onion in the olive oil in the large skillet over medium heat for 6 minutes, stirring frequently, until soft and translucent with a few pale golden edges.

doneness_cues.visual: The onion is translucent with light golden edges.
doneness_cues.tactile: The slices are soft and flexible.

instructions.text: Peel away the loosened poblano skins when the peppers are cool enough to handle. Leave occasional small flecks of char, but remove broad blackened patches.
tips: Avoid rinsing the peeled peppers, which washes away roasted flavor.

instructions.text: Slice the peeled poblano flesh into strips approximately 1 cm wide.
Stir the poblano strips, Mexican crema and salt into the softened onions over low heat until evenly combined.
Simmer the filling very gently for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce coats the strips and only small bubbles appear around the edges. Warm the tortillas during this interval.

doneness_cues.visual: The crema is glossy and clings to the peppers, with small bubbles at the edges.

tips: Keep the heat low; a rolling boil can separate the crema.

instructions.text: Warm the tortillas on the dry griddle over medium-high heat in batches, approximately 20–30 seconds per side. Stack them in the clean kitchen towel as they finish to keep them pliable.

doneness_cues.visual: The tortillas develop scattered toasted spots.
doneness_cues.tactile: Each tortilla folds easily without cracking.

instructions.text: Divide the warm poblano filling among the 12 tortillas, allowing 3 tacos per serving. Serve immediately.

troubleshooting.symptom: The crema looks grainy or separates into oily patches.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The filling boiled vigorously or cooked too long.
troubleshooting.prevention: Use full-fat Mexican crema and maintain only a gentle simmer.
troubleshooting.fix: Remove the skillet from the heat and stir gently as it cools slightly. Mild separation may improve; severely curdled crema will not become completely smooth.

troubleshooting.symptom: The poblano skins are difficult to remove.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The skins were insufficiently blistered or the peppers rested uncovered.
troubleshooting.prevention: Blacken most of the skin and rest the peppers covered immediately after broiling.
troubleshooting.fix: Scrape away stubborn loose skin with the back of the knife; leave small tender patches rather than tearing away the flesh.

chef_notes: Broiling broad pepper panels exposes the skin evenly and avoids repeatedly turning whole peppers.
Cut onions thinly so they soften during the peppers' covered rest and remain tender inside the tacos.
Poblano heat varies. Removing seeds and pale inner ribs reduces some heat but does not guarantee mild peppers.
Mexican crema supplies the defining tang and silky texture; keep its cooking time short.
Warm tortillas immediately before filling so they stay flexible and carry the sauce without cracking.
data.cultural_context: Rajas means strips, describing the cut peppers at the center of this Mexican preparation. Poblanos cooked with onions and crema are served as a vegetable dish or tucked into tortillas as a taco filling. Reference: [Creamed Rajas](https://www.epicurious.com/recipes/food/views/creamed-rajas-387019).
